stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# So rule: crop each color's bbox (trim leading/trailing zero cols/rows), then lay them out side by side horizontally sharing full height. Order? By color value ascending? or spatial order? In demo both give 2,3,8. Spatial by position of first pixel?
def f(g):
    from collections import defaultdict
    cells=defaultdict(list)
    for i,row in enumerate(g):
        for j,v in enumerate(row):
            if v: cells[v].append((i,j))
    objs=[]
    for c,ps in sorted(cells.items()):
        rs=[p[0] for p in ps]; cs=[p[1] for p in ps]
        r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)
        b=[[c if g[r][k]==c else 0 for k in range(c0,c1+1)] for r in range(r0,r1+1)]
        # trim zero edges
        while len(b)>1 and not any(x in b[-1] for x in range(10)): b.pop()
        while len(b)>1 and not any(x in b[0] for x in range(10)): b.insert(0,[0]*len(b[0]))
        while len(b[0])>1 and not any(x in b[0] for x in range(10)): b=[r[1:] for r in b]
        while len(b[0])>1 and not any(x in b[-1] for x in range(10)): b=[r[:-1] for r in b]
        objs.append((c,b))
    total=sum(len(o) for _,o in objs)
    h=max(len(o) for _,o in objs)
    out=[[0]*total for _ in range(h)]
    w=0
    for c,(b) in objs:
        for r,row in enumerate(b):
            out[r][w:w+len(row)]=row
        w+=len(b[0])
    return out
print(f(di)==do)
